solutions.explanation:
Assume \(a>0\), \(a\ne1\), \(M>0\), and \(N>0\). The logarithm of a product equals the sum of the logarithms, so
\[
\log_a(MN)=\log_a M+\log_a N.
\]
Subtraction applies to the logarithm of a quotient.

The positive-factor assumption is missing from the question. For example, if \(a=2\) and \(M=N=-1\), then \(\log_a(MN)=\log_2 1=0\), but all four choices contain undefined real logarithms. Thus A is correct under the standard positive-factor assumption; as written, no choice is valid for every input for which the left side exists.
